errors.nothingToApply: Nothing in this skin can go into the game files: only textures and material settings (metallic, smoothness, glow, colour) can.
errors.gameChanged: The game files changed meanwhile (a game update or a Steam file check). Open “Restore original game assets” to see the state, then try again.
errors.stalePatch: The game files still hold skins written for an older game version. Run “Verify integrity of game files” in Steam, then try again.
errors.badBackup: The backup of an original file is missing or damaged, so it can’t be restored. Run “Verify integrity of game files” in Steam; it puts the originals back.
gameFiles.groupInfo: No plugin needed: textures and material settings are written straight into the game’s own asset files, after backing up the originals. Attachments, screens, animated textures, sounds and layout changes can’t go in. A game update or a Steam file check puts the originals back.
gameFiles.replaceWhat: Writes the textures and material settings of “{{v0}}” straight into GTFO’s game files (the originals are backed up and can be restored at any time). No plugin needed; other players still see their own files.
gameFiles.notWritten: These can’t go into the game files and are skipped:
gameFiles.closeGame: Close the game first: it holds these files while it runs.
gameFiles.applied: Written to the game files; shows the next time the game starts
gameFiles.applyFailed: Could not write the game files
gameFiles.none: No skins are written into the game files right now.
gameFiles.restoreFailed: Could not restore the game files
gameFiles.stale: There are records from an older game version. After a game update those backups can’t be used; verify the game files in Steam, then clear these records.
gameFiles.exportFailed: Could not export the game asset pack

welcome.title: Welcome to ForgeSkin
welcome.pickInfo: Click the weapon name at the top left to change weapon. Each weapon can have several skins; switch them in the skin strip above.
welcome.lookInfo: Click a part on the left; the icon bar on the right has textures, livery and dynamic layers. You can also drop a whole texture folder into the window.
welcome.attachInfo: Ammo screens, imported models and hologram shapes mount on parts; the Simulate buttons at the bottom preview kills, shots and other events with their animations, effects and sounds.
welcome.applyInfo: Choose an r2modman profile and click Apply to game at the top right; the plugin installs itself, and while the game runs changes hot-reload into it.
welcome.exampleDone: The example skin is ready: a painted {{v0}}, an ammo screen and a hologram ring. Open them on the left to see how each is set up.

gameLog.notMultiple: Texture “{{v0}}” is not a multiple of 4 in size, so the game keeps it uncompressed (more video memory)
gameLog.updateFailed: “{{v0}}” failed to refresh and stays as it was: {{v1}}
gameLog.sameId: Two skins share one id ({{v0}}); only one is used
gameLog.noReply: Installed into the test profile, but the game did not answer within a few seconds. Open “Game log” to see why.
gameLog.title: Game log
gameLog.empty: Nothing yet. Once the game runs, what the skin plugin writes shows up here.
addMenu.title: Add to this part
leftRail.pendingInfo: Some textures were matched with low confidence. Click to confirm them.
partModel.title: Model
partModel.info: Replace this node’s model with your own .glb. Only its own model changes: child parts stay, textures and materials still apply, and position, rotation and scale stay editable.
topBar.testProfileInfo: “Apply to game” installs only into this profile, for your own testing, and turns on live refresh in game. To give the skin to others, use “Publish”.
topBar.autoApplyInfo: While the game runs, applies to the game 2 seconds after each change and only speaks up when something goes wrong.
actions.pluginMissing: The skin plugin is not installed.
actions.pluginWrong: The skin plugin is the wrong version.
livery.title: Livery
livery.info: Like a racing game's livery editor: pick a finish, then stack base coats, decals and brush strokes. Layers higher in the list sit on top. Packing bakes everything into the part's textures, so the game sees ordinary textures, and “Replace game files” works too.
livery.finishInfo: Sets how metallic and glossy the part looks. It makes the part's metallic/smoothness texture; Glow makes the paint itself light up.
livery.empty: No paint layers yet. Add one with the buttons above.
livery.blendInfo: Normal covers what is below. Multiply only darkens and keeps the detail below (use it for a base coat that keeps the original texture). Screen only lightens. Overlay boosts contrast. Add brightens like light.
livery.depthInfo: How far the decal prints into and out from the surface. Too much prints on the far side of the part; too little cuts it off on curves.
livery.placeHint: In the 3D view, press on this part and drag: the decal slides along the surface and turns with its curves.
livery.notPlaced: Not placed yet: click this part in the 3D view.
livery.brushHint: Drag on the part in the 3D view to paint; pick the shape and width in the bar over the view.
livery.maskInfo: Wherever the mask is painted, this layer is hidden. Turn on “Paint mask” and drag in the 3D view.
livery.bar.decal: Drag on the part: move the decal
livery.bar.mask: Drag on the part: paint the mask
livery.bar.fill: Turn on Paint mask to keep areas free of this coat
livery.playbackHint: {{v0}} frames. In game the decal plays like a dynamic layer; until it plays it shows its first frame. Paint above and below it is baked into every frame.
livery.badImage: This image cannot be opened. Try a PNG or JPG.
errors.noLiveryView: The livery is baked in the 3D view: wait until the weapon shows there, then try again.
errors.duplicateMaterial: Two overrides edit the same material: keep one of them and try again.
errors.fileInUse: Another program has the file open: close it and try again.
shapes.title: Shapes
hologram.title: Hologram
hologram.info: Drawn in game as a glowing, flickering hologram with the game's own hologram shader, in the model's colour and the screen's colours.
topBar.developerInfo: Shows the log panel and the game log; while the game runs, problems in game (a part left without the skin, for one) go into the log and pop up at the bottom right. Off, logs are still written to the log file and only errors show.
topBar.update.dev: A development run does not update; the installed app checks
topBar.update.downloading: A new version is downloading in the background; you will be asked to restart when it is ready
topBar.update.error: Could not check for updates; check the network and try again
exportMod.formatForge: ForgeSkin format: every effect (dynamic layers, attachments, sounds, part changes), applied by the ForgeSkin plugin.
exportMod.formatSkins: Skins format: for players with the Skins library (food-Skins). Still textures and material settings only; dynamic layers, attachments, sounds and part changes are left out.
exportMod.doneDropped: Thunderstore skin mod exported; {{v0}} things the Skins format cannot carry are listed in the log
skins.notGroup: Pick the manifest.skingroup.json in the skin group folder
app.updateReady: A new version is downloaded; restart ForgeSkin to use it (the plugin updates too).
app.filesChanged: Files changed outside the editor, read again: {{v0}}
livery.wearInfo: Wears the paint below away by the model’s edges, bumps and random patches, showing the game’s own texture and metal. Edges go first.
livery.killsToFullInfo: 0 = fixed wear. Above 0 the gun starts clean and wears in four stages with your kills with it, reaching the amount above at this many kills. Kills are counted per skin and gun.
variants.title: Colour variants
variants.info: Several colourings of one skin. With one selected, livery colour edits change only it. Apply uses the selected one; an exported mod has each as its own skin (named “ · variant”).
swing.title: Charm swing
swing.info: Hang this attachment as a charm from its origin (the model's -Y points down at rest); in game it swings with the gear's moves, turns and gravity. The 3D view swings it the same way when you move it or press Shake.
stickers.title: Stickers
livery.shape.fill: Fill a piece (click: the whole UV island is painted or masked)
livery.mirrorInfo: Also paints the mirror image on the gear's other side (across its centre plane); fills too
skins.title: Skins
playerColors.title: Player colours
playerColors.info: Colours players can change themselves in game, in the skin picker. One player colour can drive several places (say the body tint and the screen digits); they always change together.
playerColors.empty: None yet. Click the person button next to a colour to let players change it.
playerColors.name: Name
playerColors.paletteInfo: Offered first in the game's picker; players can still pick any colour. Click one to try it here.
playerColors.remove: Players can no longer change this
playerColors.toggle: Let players change this colour in game
swing.shakeInfo: Jolts the gear sideways so the charms swing as they do in game
